entries.title: Irving and Zvi rebut Scott Alexander's 'Against SURA' on unilateral pauses
entries.summary: Irving argues Alexander attacks a strawman. Stronger plans use conditional or limited unilateral pauses: training resumes if others do not pause, and staff move to alignment and product work. He says the game theory is not simple. Zvi calls Alexander's claims poor.
entries.analysis: Live pause-strategy debate with direct game-theory content for treaty design.

entries.title: IAPS: How to Secure Advanced U.S. Chips
entries.summary: IAPS argues US chip export controls have gaps in rules and enforcement. It urges a ban on remote access to controlled chips, anti-smuggling mechanisms for China, limits on H200 licences, and allied tightening of chipmaking equipment controls.
entries.analysis: Concrete enforcement and verification-adjacent proposals on US-China chip controls.
